points.description: States that overloaded functions are differentiated by their function signature, i.e. the parameter list (number, types and/or order of parameters), using the term 'signature' or an explicit parameter-list equivalent.
points.partial_credit: Half: says differentiated by parameters (number or types) but does not use the term signature or name both number and type/order.

points.description: States that when an overloaded function is called, the compiler selects/finds the function whose signature is closest (best match) to the arguments given in the call.
points.partial_credit: Half: says the compiler matches the call to a function by its arguments but does not say best/closest match.

rubric.notes: Full marks need both the term 'signature' (or precise parameter-list wording) and the closest-match selection at call time. Vague answers such as 'by the name' or 'by the compiler' earn nothing; saying differentiation is by return type or name alone is wrong and loses P1. Part marks only where clearly more than half of a point is precisely stated.
